title: the Pandavas' last journey, Yudhishthira's dog, heaven
hook: Arjuna falls, then Bhima, who asks with his last breath why he is falling
carry: you ate without a thought for others
tomorrow: the Pandavas' last journey, Yudhishthira's dog, heaven

segments.voice: Yesterday the twins fell: Sahadeva for thinking no one his equal in wisdom, Nakula in beauty. Your line was no one is equal to me.

Arjuna, who threw his bow into the sea, is still walking. He's the one who heard the Gita in the chariot, who won Draupadi at her bridegroom-choice, who fought through the war. Then, on the high road, grief at his brothers' falling seems to catch up with him, and Arjuna falls too. Bhima, who has asked why each time, asks again. A little later Bhima the strong feels his own legs go, and lying on the ground, he calls out one more question, this time about himself.
screen: `ARJUNA STILL WALKING.` → `ARJUNA FALLS.` → `BHIMA ASKS ABOUT HIMSELF.`

segments.voice: About Arjuna, Yudhishthira's answer in Ganguli's telling has two parts. Arjuna once said he would destroy all their enemies in a single day, and he didn't. And he looked down on other bowmen. A boast that went unkept, and a habit of disregard. Then Bhima falls, and this time he asks about no one else: I'm falling too. Why? Yudhishthira answers him directly. You ate too much, he says, you boasted of your strength, and you ate without a thought for what others needed. Then he walks on. Now look back down this whole road. Draupadi, the twins, Arjuna, Bhima. Each fall comes with a reason, and each reason is small and specific: a heart that leaned, a comparison, a boast, an appetite. Not one of them is a great crime. These are people who did great things and, in this telling, carried one ordinary weight too many up a mountain. One more detail. Bhima, the brother who kept stopping to look, is the last to fall before Yudhishthira is alone. The question why goes with him. The text leaves no verdict on the verdicts, only an image: one man, still walking, toward the top of the world. And behind him, the only one left, not a brother, not a queen: the dog.
screen: `ARJUNA: AN UNKEPT BOAST` · `BHIMA: "WHY AM I FALLING?"` · `EACH REASON SMALL AND SPECIFIC` · then, large: `ONE MAN WALKING, AND A DOG`

segments.voice: Let your breath settle low and gently ask Bhima's question of yourself: what's one ordinary weight I'm carrying that I don't need, an old boast, a grudge, a habit of too much? Let just one come, name it on the in-breath, set it down on the path on the out-breath, and sit with the lighter feeling without hurrying on. If you pray, you can offer that weight in your prayer.
Bhima. The second Pandava, the strong one, who asks why each traveler falls, and falls last himself before Yudhishthira walks on with only the dog.
Your line: you ate without a thought for others. Now only Yudhishthira and the dog walk on. Day eight hundred seventy-six, done.
